concept.name: Structured output
concept.definition: Model output constrained to follow a declared machine-readable format — typically JSON conforming to a schema — rather than free-form prose, so downstream systems can parse, validate, and route it deterministically. JSON Schema is the standard declarative language for describing the required structure and constraints.
concept.intuition: Instead of an essay you must re-read, make the model fill in a form with fixed fields, so software can consume the answer directly.
concept.mechanics: The caller supplies a schema (field names, types, required properties, allowed values); the model is prompted or constrained (via grammar-guided or schema-constrained decoding) to emit conforming JSON; a validator then checks the instance against the schema before the data is used.
concept.failure_modes: Schema-conformant output can still be semantically wrong — validation checks shape, not truth. Long or deeply nested schemas raise the rate of truncation and subtle type errors, and models may hallucinate field values to satisfy required fields.
concept.misconceptions: Getting valid JSON is not the same as getting a correct answer; structured output solves the parsing problem, not the reliability problem. Prompting alone ('please reply in JSON') is not a guarantee — only schema-constrained decoding or post-hoc validation enforces it.
concept.example: A strategy-review agent must return {"verdict": "pass|fail", "issues": [...], "citations": [...]}; the orchestrator rejects any response failing schema validation instead of trying to parse prose.
